name: Sentinel Bio (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: the grants, the recipients read live and the advised gift all work against pandemics, which kill people everywhere, and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: Sentinel Bio (Washington DC, founded 2024) pools philanthropists' money and grants it for work against catastrophic pandemics, mostly on screening orders for synthetic DNA and on AI tools that can design biology; this model covers all it spent in its first tax year, May to December 2024 ($1.53M, $1.11M of it grants made in November and December), and the $1.08M it advised another donor to give the Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security. At the defaults it averts about 4.7 years of healthy life per $1,000 (0.4 to 60 on the combined range): about half from three grants valued as a typical dollar of pandemic work (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), a fifth from two fellowships counted through the work they add to the field, a quarter from its grant to the Council on Strategic Risks, read at that charity's figure on this site, and a few percent from the advised gift, valued as money shifted to a better use; its own costs (28% of the spending) count only through the grants and advice they buy. The biggest uncertainty is how much a dollar of such work cuts the risk (Rethink calls its figures placeholders; the range runs ten times either way); the result also moves with the discount rate, the years a cut counts and what its next dollar does (49%: its reserves were six years of 2024's spending, but its grants have since grown several times over). Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the grants or the advice on the risk is measured.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

rows.label: AI: deaths averted a year by a typical $1 million of work, while its cut counts
rows.formula: ((1 - ai_misuse_cost_share) * @catastrophe.ai_extinction_cut_per_million + ai_misuse_cost_share * @catastrophe.ai_misuse_extinction_cut_per_million) * ai_extinction_per_year * deaths_if_extinct + ((1 - ai_misuse_cost_share) * @catastrophe.ai_catastrophe_cut_per_million + ai_misuse_cost_share * @catastrophe.ai_misuse_catastrophe_cut_per_million) * (ai_catastrophe_per_year * ai_deaths_if_catastrophe + ai_smaller_per_year * ai_smaller_deaths)
rows.explainer: The share of each yearly risk a typical $1 million of work in the area removes (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, its backfire step included; shared), × the deaths that risk carries: misuse work at Rethink's misuse preset, other AI work at its misalignment preset, weighted by ai_misuse_cost_share. The catastrophe figure also applies to the smaller size. Fixed; don't edit.

rows.label: AI: future healthy years kept a year by a typical $1 million of work
rows.explainer: As ai_deaths_per_million, for the future lost in an extinction-level catastrophe: the two presets' extinction cuts weighted by ai_misuse_cost_share.

rows.label: Pandemic field work: how far the typical project's effect applies
rows.explainer: The three grants fund typical pandemic policy research (the cut per dollar is a typical project's): a method for stress-testing DNA order screening (the Engineering Biology Research Consortium, with providers), a European roadmap for nucleic acid governance (Resilience Action Network International, in consultation with providers and EU bodies), and a customer-verification system (an independent researcher). Their outputs were still to come at the end of 2024, and in 2025 and 2026 Sentinel funded follow-ups (EBRC and IBBIS's auditable customer-screening standard; rani again in 2025 and 2026), a sign the first rounds were taken up; but no uptake by providers or governments is measured. 0.8, our judgment, 0.3 to 1.2, as for IBBIS's synthesis-screening work (0.8) and Ploughshares Fund's grants (0.8): a grantmaker's choice of work at a chokepoint (synthesis screening) is not counted above a typical project without measured uptake.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of the grants on the risk is measured; the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the adjustments are judgments, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12), to the pandemic grants and the fellowships here and to the advised gift through informed_money_value; the grants read at their recipients' figures take each recipient's own step (destination_reads).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above, for the branches on the typical-project chain (the pandemic grants and the fellowships). The grants read at their recipients' figures and the advised gift carry their own models' adjustments and are added after (outcome_total).

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the pandemics counted, for the grants and fellowships on the typical-project chain: synthesis screening and customer checks also stop orders for toxins, whose misuse kills few rather than starts a pandemic, and the fellowships connect protein-design researchers with policy. +5%, from 0 to +15%, our judgment, as in our IBBIS model (+5%).

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: A typical project's chance of backfiring is already in the shared cut. The grants build no capabilities: screening methods, governance roadmaps and customer checks only restrict access. 0, down to −2% if screening rules push legitimate orders to providers that don't screen. Our judgment, as for IBBIS.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire: stress-testing screening systems finds ways around them, which, if published, shows a would-be attacker how to order dangerous sequences unflagged (the EBRC study is run with providers so the gaps can be closed first). −3%, from −10% to 0, our judgment, as for IBBIS and SecureBio (−3%).
